scenario.title: Smoke, Sparks & Heartbeats
scenario.description: A grill chain, a power company, a smart-home maker and a heart-monitor lab compete for your money in the Republic of Valdoria. Read the news, watch for delayed effects and keep enough cash for rent.

companies.name: Sizzle & Co.
companies.description: A family-founded grill chain with 64 restaurants across Valdoria. Famous for smoky burgers, late-night opening hours and a pepper sauce nobody has managed to copy. Restaurants buy their meat and grain on monthly contracts.
companies.condition: Steady and profitable. Meat and grain make up almost half of its costs, so food prices matter a lot.

companies.name: Voltara Power
companies.main_product: Electricity from wind farms and hydro plants
companies.description: The biggest electricity supplier in the northern provinces. Runs 12 wind farms and two mountain hydro plants, and sells power to homes and businesses on long contracts.
companies.condition: Reliable and a bit boring - in a good way. Pays regular dividends, but depends on energy prices and government rules.

companies.name: PixelNest
companies.description: A fast-growing smart-home company that makes thermostats, door sensors and the app that connects them. Every product is built in one large factory on the edge of Port Lumen.
companies.condition: Growing fast, but it borrowed a lot of money and relies on a single factory for everything it sells.

companies.name: MediPulse Labs
companies.description: A research-driven lab that designs wrist-worn heart monitors. Hospitals use them to watch patients after surgery; families use them to keep an eye on grandparents at home.
companies.condition: Promising products waiting for regulator approval. Strong research team, modest profits so far.

events.title: Record harvest: meat and grain prices tumble
events.description: Valdoria's farmers report their best season in 20 years. Wholesale prices for beef, chicken and wheat fell 18% this week. Supermarkets expect cheaper shelves soon, while restaurants still buy on monthly contracts.

effects.consequence_text: The drop in meat and grain prices from 2 weeks ago finally reached restaurant kitchens. Food costs fell, margins grew - and Sizzle & Co. shares followed.

events.title: PixelNest unveils the HeatSmart thermostat
events.description: PixelNest's new thermostat promises to cut home heating bills by a quarter. More than 40,000 people pre-ordered it in the first 48 hours.

effects.consequence_text: Investors loved the HeatSmart pre-orders - PixelNest shares rose the same week.

events.title: Celebrity chef: 'Burgers are so last season'
events.description: TV chef Rocco Vantelli told a talk show that burgers are 'out' and that 'everyone will be eating foam and moss by spring'. The clip has 3 million views.

events.title: Parliament raises the energy excise tax
events.description: Lawmakers voted to raise the excise tax on electricity and gas by 20%, starting next week. Landlords warn that the cost of heating and lighting buildings will be passed on to tenants.

effects.consequence_text: The energy excise voted in Week 2 just reached your landlord's bills - your monthly rent went up by $80.
Investors worried that pricier energy means customers will use less of it - Voltara shares slipped right away.

events.title: MediPulse files its new heart monitor for approval
events.description: MediPulse sent its PulseBand 2 monitor to the national health regulator. Approval usually takes a couple of weeks. Doctors who tested it call it 'the most accurate wristband we have seen'.

effects.consequence_text: Hopeful investors bought a little MediPulse right after the filing.
The PulseBand 2 filed in Week 2 has just been approved. MediPulse can now sell it to hospitals - and its share price jumped.

events.title: Viral post: 'Wind turbines scare away the clouds'
events.description: A post claiming that Voltara's wind turbines 'push rain clouds away' was shared 500,000 times. Weather scientists call it complete nonsense.

events.title: Fire at PixelNest's only factory
events.description: A fire broke out overnight at PixelNest's factory in Port Lumen. Nobody was hurt, but the production lines are badly damaged and all HeatSmart deliveries are on hold.

effects.consequence_text: The factory fire hit PixelNest immediately - investors sold the same week, expecting months without sales.
With its only factory offline and loans to repay, PixelNest's bankruptcy risk jumped.

events.title: Weather service warns of a long heatwave
events.description: Forecasters expect record temperatures for the next few weeks. Shops report that air conditioners are selling out across Valdoria.

effects.consequence_text: The heatwave forecast in Week 3 arrived - air conditioners ran day and night, Voltara sold more electricity and its shares rose.

events.title: Rumor: a foreign giant wants to buy Sizzle & Co.
events.description: An anonymous forum user claims a huge foreign food group is about to buy Sizzle & Co. at a big premium. Neither company has commented.

events.title: Voltara reports a record quarter
events.description: Voltara earned more than ever this quarter. The board announced that dividend payments to shareholders will go up starting next week.

effects.consequence_text: Record profits lifted Voltara's share price as soon as the results were published.
The bigger dividend promised in Week 4 kicked in - Voltara now pays shareholders more cash every week.

events.title: PixelNest's insurer disputes the fire claim
events.description: PixelNest's insurance company says the factory's sprinklers were not properly maintained and may refuse to pay for the damage. Lawyers expect a long fight.

effects.consequence_text: News of the insurance dispute pushed PixelNest shares lower right away.
The insurance dispute from Week 4 turned into real cash trouble - without a payout, PixelNest's bankruptcy risk climbed again.

events.title: Gossip: MediPulse boss spotted on a luxury yacht
events.description: A celebrity magazine printed blurry photos of someone who 'looks like' MediPulse's founder at a yacht party. The company says she was at a medical conference that day.

events.title: Restaurant workers win a higher minimum wage
events.description: After long negotiations, restaurant staff in Valdoria will earn 12% more starting next week. Owners say they will have to raise menu prices or accept smaller profits.

effects.consequence_text: The higher wages agreed in Week 5 showed up in restaurant costs - Sizzle & Co.'s profits shrank and its share price dipped.
Bigger wage bills from Week 5 made Sizzle & Co. trim its dividend by a quarter.

events.title: Bank cuts PixelNest's credit line
events.description: Valdoria Merchant Bank halved the amount PixelNest is allowed to borrow. Without new money, the company may struggle to pay suppliers and rebuild its factory.

effects.consequence_text: Losing its bank credit sent PixelNest shares down immediately.
The credit cut from Week 5 left PixelNest unable to pay its bills - its bankruptcy risk crossed the danger line.

events.title: Astrologer: 'A golden week for energy stocks'
events.description: A popular astrologer told her 2 million followers that 'Jupiter is smiling on energy companies' this week.

events.title: MediPulse signs an export deal with three countries
events.description: Hospitals in Kestria, Nordhavia and the Solmara Islands will buy PulseBand 2 monitors for the next two years - MediPulse's biggest deal ever.

effects.consequence_text: The export deal lifted MediPulse shares the same week it was announced.

events.title: Regulator caps electricity prices for winter
events.description: The energy regulator limited how much power companies may charge households this winter. Customers cheer; energy companies grumble.

effects.consequence_text: A cap on electricity prices means smaller profits ahead - Voltara shares dipped right away.

events.title: Online trend: 'Smart fridges are spying on your snacks'
events.description: A viral video jokes that smart-home devices secretly count how many snacks you eat. Tech reviewers point out that the video is satire.

w1-noise-chef.reveal: One TV chef's opinion doesn't change how many burgers people actually buy. Sizzle & Co.'s sales were not affected.

w2-noise-clouds.reveal: Wind turbines don't move clouds. A viral post isn't evidence - always ask who is behind a claim.

w3-noise-takeover.reveal: No buyer ever showed up - the 'takeover' was an anonymous rumor. If Sizzle & Co. rose this week, it was thanks to the cheap meat from Week 1.

w4-noise-yacht.reveal: A blurry gossip photo says nothing about how a company is doing. MediPulse's founder was at a medical conference.

w5-noise-astro.reveal: Horoscopes don't set share prices. Anything that happened to Voltara came from real news - like its record quarter and bigger dividend.

w6-noise-fridge.reveal: The video was a joke. PixelNest's real problems were the factory fire, the insurance dispute and its bank debt - not snack-counting fridges.

week_lesson.title_delayed: Old news just hit the market
week_lesson.title_quiet: A calm week on the market
week_lesson.summary_no_moves: Share prices barely moved this week.
week_lesson.lag_with_delayed: Markets don't always react the moment news breaks. Restaurants buy food on monthly contracts, new laws start later and bills arrive weeks after a decision - so an effect can land long after the headline. This week: {items}.
week_lesson.lag_without_delayed: Nothing from older news landed this week - but stay alert. Some headlines need one, two or even three weeks to reach a company's costs, its profits or your own bills. Re-read earlier news before you trade.
week_lesson.immediate_note: Some news moved prices the very same week: {items}.
week_lesson.noise_note: Not every headline matters: {items} turned out to be noise and changed nothing.
week_lesson.rent_change_note: Your monthly rent changed by {delta} (now {rent}) because of news from Week {source_week}.
week_lesson.rent_paid_note: You paid {amount} in rent this week.
week_lesson.dividend_note: Your shares paid you {amount} in dividends - cash just for owning them.
week_lesson.bankruptcy_note: {names} went bankrupt. Its shares are now worth $0 and can no longer be traded.
week_lesson.takeaway_delayed: Today's headline can be next month's price move. Before you trade, look back at older news.
week_lesson.takeaway_immediate: Big surprises, like disasters, hit prices right away. Spreading your money across companies softens the blow.
week_lesson.takeaway_quiet: Calm weeks are a good moment to check your plan and your cash reserve for upcoming bills.

glossary.Market lag: The delay between a piece of news and its effect on prices. Some news needs weeks to show up.
glossary.Dividend: Cash a company pays to its shareholders, just for owning its shares.
glossary.Share price: What one small piece of a company costs right now.
glossary.Bankruptcy risk: How likely a company is to run out of money. If it goes bankrupt, its shares can become worthless.
glossary.Liquidity: How much cash you can use right away - for example, to pay your rent.
glossary.Noise: News that sounds important but doesn't actually change anything.
glossary.Diversification: Spreading your money across different companies and industries, so one bad event can't sink you.
glossary.ROI: Return on investment: how much your money grew or shrank, shown in percent.
glossary.Excise tax: An extra tax on specific products, such as fuel or electricity.

advisor.accurate_delayed: Keep an eye on {company} ({ticker}). '{event}' could {direction} its price {timing}. Markets often need time to catch up with news.
advisor.accurate_immediate: '{event}' looks important for {company} ({ticker}). I'd expect it to {direction} the price {timing}.
advisor.accurate_risk: Careful with {company} ({ticker}). After '{event}', its money problems look serious - if a company goes bankrupt, its shares can be worth nothing.
advisor.accurate_dividend: '{event}' could change how much {company} ({ticker}) pays its shareholders {timing}. Dividends add up week after week.
advisor.accurate_rent: '{event}' may not move share prices much, but it could make your bills bigger {timing}. Keep some cash ready for rent.
advisor.misleading_noise: Big news! '{event}' could really {direction} the price of {company} ({ticker}) - and fast. If I were you, I'd act this week.
advisor.misleading_inverted: I have a feeling about {company} ({ticker}): after '{event}', I think the market will {direction} its price. Trust me on this one.
advisor.quiet_week: Honestly, I don't see anything big this week. Sometimes the smartest move is to stick to your plan and keep cash for bills.

cautious.label: Cautious Saver
cautious.description: You kept most of your money in cash. That's safe and kept your bills covered, but cash alone doesn't grow or earn dividends.

balanced.label: Balanced Diversifier
balanced.description: You spread your money across several companies and kept some cash aside. That's how many long-term investors protect themselves from surprises.

concentrated.label: Focused Bettor
concentrated.description: You put most of your money into one company at a time. When the pick is right it pays off big - but one bad headline can hurt a lot.

aggressive.label: Bold Go-Getter
aggressive.description: You kept nearly all your money invested and traded often. Bold moves can pay off, but they leave little room for bills and surprises.

reactive.label: Headline Chaser
reactive.description: You reacted quickly to the news - including headlines that turned out to be noise. Speed only helps when the news is real.

diversify.title: Spread your bets
diversify.tip: Own a few companies from different industries. One fire, lawsuit or bad quarter shouldn't sink your whole savings.

cash_reserve.title: Keep a bill buffer
cash_reserve.tip: Before investing, set aside enough cash for upcoming bills like rent. Money you'll need soon shouldn't be stuck in shares.

delayed_signals.title: Read yesterday's news
delayed_signals.tip: Many effects arrive late - contracts, laws and prices take weeks to pass through. Ask: 'What happened two weeks ago that hasn't shown up yet?'

noise.title: Check the source
noise.tip: Rumors, gossip and viral posts are usually noise. Ask who is saying it and whether it changes the company's real sales or costs.

bankruptcy.title: Respect the warning lights
bankruptcy.tip: When a company's bankruptcy risk keeps climbing, shrink your stake. A cheap-looking share can still fall to zero.

dividends.title: Let dividends work for you
dividends.tip: Steady companies that pay dividends hand you cash regularly - even in weeks when prices stand still.

advisor.title: Trust, but verify
advisor.tip: Advisors and experts can be wrong. Treat a hint as one opinion and compare it with the actual news before you act.

patience.title: Have a plan, not a reflex
patience.tip: Decide why you are buying before you buy. A few well-reasoned trades usually beat many quick ones.

final_analysis.overall_positive: You finished with {net_worth} - a {roi} return. Great job turning headlines into decisions!
final_analysis.overall_neutral: You finished with {net_worth} ({roi}). You protected your money - next time, let's make it grow a little smarter.
final_analysis.overall_negative: You finished with {net_worth} ({roi}). Losing money in a game is the cheapest way to learn - here is what to try next time.
final_analysis.overall_liquidity: You ran out of cash for rent in Week {week}. That ends the game - but it's one of the most valuable lessons in personal finance: bills come first.

s_diversified.title: You spread your money out
s_diversified.detail: You owned {count} different companies across {industries} industries. When one stock stumbled, the others cushioned the fall.

s_caught_delayed.title: You were in place before old news hit
s_caught_delayed.detail: You held {shares} {ticker} shares when '{event}' (Week {source_week}) finally moved the price in Week {trigger_week} ({impact}). That's how patient investors profit from market lag.

s_dodged_delayed.title: You dodged a delayed hit
s_dodged_delayed.detail: You sold {ticker} after '{event}' appeared in Week {source_week} - before it pulled the price down in Week {trigger_week}.

s_cash_reserve.title: You kept cash for the bills
s_cash_reserve.detail: You had {cash} in cash before the {rent} rent payment in Week {week}. The bill never caught you off guard.

s_exited_risk.title: You left a sinking ship in time
s_exited_risk.detail: You sold your {ticker} shares before the company went bankrupt in Week {week}.

s_avoided_bankrupt.title: You avoided the bankruptcy
s_avoided_bankrupt.detail: You held no {ticker} shares when it went bankrupt in Week {week}. Watching the risk meter pays off.

s_ignored_noise.title: You didn't fall for the noise
s_ignored_noise.detail: None of your trades followed the {count} misleading headlines. Staying calm when rumors fly is a real skill.

s_dividends.title: Your shares paid you
s_dividends.detail: You collected {amount} in dividends - money that arrived without selling a single share.

s_profit.title: You grew your money
s_profit.detail: You finished with {net_worth}, a return of {roi}, after paying all your bills.

s_finished.title: You stayed in the game
s_finished.detail: You made it through all {weeks} weeks and saw how news, delays and bills shape your money.

i_concentrated.title: Too many eggs in one basket
i_concentrated.detail: At one point {share} of your stock money sat in {ticker} alone. Spreading across industries limits the damage when one company gets hit.

i_missed_delayed.title: The early signal was there
i_missed_delayed.detail: '{event}' appeared in Week {source_week}, but {ticker} only reacted in Week {trigger_week} ({impact}). Buying in between would have caught that move.

i_hit_delayed.title: Old news caught up with you
i_hit_delayed.detail: You held {shares} {ticker} shares when '{event}' from Week {source_week} pulled the price down in Week {trigger_week} ({impact}). Re-reading older headlines could have warned you.

i_immediate_hit.title: One shock, a big dent
i_immediate_hit.detail: You held {shares} {ticker} shares when '{event}' hit in Week {week} and lost about {loss}. Owning several companies would have softened the blow.

i_low_cash.title: Rent nearly caught you
i_low_cash.detail: Before the {rent} rent payment in Week {week} you had only {cash} in cash. Keep a cushion for bills you know are coming.

i_liquidity.title: Out of cash on rent day
i_liquidity.detail: After paying {rent} rent in Week {week} your cash fell to {cash}. Shares are not cash - sell in time or keep a reserve.

i_bankrupt_loss.title: Held on until the very end
i_bankrupt_loss.detail: You still owned {shares} {ticker} shares when it went bankrupt in Week {week} - about {loss} turned into $0. A 'Critical' risk label is a signal to reduce your stake.

i_followed_noise.title: A rumor moved your money
i_followed_noise.detail: In Week {week} you {action} {ticker} right after '{event}' - a headline that turned out to be noise.

i_followed_bad_advice.title: The advisor got it wrong
i_followed_bad_advice.detail: In Week {week} the advisor's hint about {ticker} was a misread, and you {action} after it. Even experts are wrong sometimes - double-check hints against the news.

i_idle_cash.title: Your cash sat on the bench
i_idle_cash.detail: On average only {share} of your money was invested. Cash is safe, but it doesn't grow or pay dividends.

i_overtrading.title: Lots of trades, lots of noise
i_overtrading.detail: You made {count} trades in {weeks} weeks. Frequent trading often means reacting to every headline instead of following a plan.

i_next_level.title: Next level: plan around delays
i_next_level.detail: Next time, write down which news could matter later and check it every week. Timing your moves around market lag is the next skill to master.
